description: Say who runs an email address and which servers to connect it with, before you connect it. We read the address's domain, then its MX records, then its published mail servers (SRV records), and nothing else: no mail server is dialed, no login is tried and no outside service is asked. `provider` is the provider's id (such as `google`, `microsoft`, `zoho` or `yahoo`) or `other`, with its `name`, `account` (`personal` for an address like gmail.com, `organization` for your own domain on that provider, null when both use the same servers) and `region`, when its servers differ by data center. `servers` holds the imap and smtp hosts, ports and security to start from, or null when none is known. `password` says which password those servers take (`normal`, `app_password`, `app_password_with_2fa`, or `secure_mail_key`, AT&T's name for its app password), `signIn` the sign-in that replaces it (`google` or `microsoft`), `accessSwitch` the setting to switch on at the provider first (`imap` for IMAP access, `third_party` for access by other email apps), and `unavailable` why no login of ours reaches this account at all (`needs_bridge`, `no_imap`, or `sign_in_unsupported`, a personal Microsoft account such as Outlook.com on a server that takes work or school accounts only). `source` says where the answer came from (`address`, `mx`, `srv` or `none`); `none` comes with `unresolved`, `not_published` or `dns_unanswered` (DNS did not answer: try again, or type the servers). A host is never guessed: when nothing is found, `servers` is null. At most 20 a minute per workspace.
name: detect_mailbox_settings
title: Detect a mailbox's settings
